scenarioContext: Person with depression trying to get out of bed in the morning. Core challenges: activation energy, self-attack patterns, all-or-nothing thinking, inertia, self-negotiation, and finding workable next steps when everything feels too hard. The scenario is about micro-momentum, not dramatic breakthroughs.
coachingFocus: Activation barriers: how depression makes simple tasks feel impossible
Self-attack vs self-compassion: different inner voices lead to different outcomes
All-or-nothing thinking: the trap of 'if I can't do everything, why do anything'
Threshold lowering: finding the smallest possible step that still counts
Recovery after setback: falling back into bed doesn't have to be permanent
Partial progress as real progress: redefining success for low-energy days
Connection and support: using others as activation scaffolding
Metacognition: noticing thought patterns while they're happening
debriefPrompts: What was the hardest moment—where did you feel most stuck?
Did you notice the self-attack voice? What did it say?
What was the smallest step you found that actually worked?
If you collapsed back, what helped you try again (or what would have helped)?
What does 'enough' look like on a day like this?
Did reaching out or accepting support feel different than going it alone?

skillSignals.description: Ability to begin movement despite heavy resistance
Finding the minimum viable action that still counts as progress
Using kinder self-talk instead of harsh criticism
Awareness of thought patterns while experiencing them
Getting back up after falling back into shutdown
Tendency toward perfectionist thinking that undermines partial wins
Willingness to reach out for support when struggling
Knowing when to push and when to rest
Letting partial effort be enough without shame

activation.whenStrong: You broke through the inertia. That's the hardest part. Use this skill in other stuck moments.
activation.whenWeak: The activation barrier was too high. Tomorrow, try setting up scaffolding the night before.
activation.practiceHint: Before bed, put one thing in place to make tomorrow's first step easier.

threshold_lowering.whenStrong: You found the smallest workable step. This skill works everywhere depression creates barriers.
threshold_lowering.whenWeak: You set the bar too high. Ask: What's even smaller? Can I do 10% of that?
threshold_lowering.practiceHint: Whatever step you're planning, ask: What's the minimum viable version?

self_compassion.whenStrong: You used a kinder voice. That's strategic, not soft. Criticism paralyzes; kindness mobilizes.
self_compassion.whenWeak: The self-attack voice won. It feels true but it's a trap.
self_compassion.practiceHint: When the critic starts, name it: 'That's the attack voice.' Then try something else.

recovery.whenStrong: You came back after falling. That's one of the rarest and most valuable skills.
recovery.whenWeak: When you fell back, you stayed down. Recovery is learnable.
recovery.practiceHint: If you collapse, set a 5-minute timer. When it goes off, try one smaller step.

persistence.whenStrong: You kept going through the heaviness. That builds capacity for next time.
persistence.whenWeak: You stopped before you wanted to. Tomorrow, try committing to one more step than feels possible.
persistence.practiceHint: When you want to stop, commit to 2 more minutes. Just 2.

support_seeking.whenStrong: You used connection. Depression says isolate; support is acting against the illness.
support_seeking.whenWeak: You went it alone when support was available. Asking isn't weakness—it's data.
support_seeking.practiceHint: Set up a morning check-in text with someone before you go to sleep.

micro_progress.detected: You built momentum through tiny steps. This is how activation works in depression.
micro_progress.nextStep: Apply this in another area: find the smallest possible step and start there.

threshold_lowered.detected: You found the minimum viable version. This skill transfers to any stuck moment.
threshold_lowered.nextStep: Before your next hard task, ask: What's 10% of this?

recovery_success.detected: You came back after collapse. Most people stay down. You didn't.
recovery_success.nextStep: Trust this skill. If you fall tomorrow, remember: the second try is always available.

compassion_applied.detected: You used a kinder voice instead of the critic. That's real work.
compassion_applied.nextStep: Notice when you're yelling at yourself. Try something else instead.

support_utilized.detected: You used connection to enable action. That's strength, not weakness.
support_utilized.nextStep: Set up support systems before you need them. Morning check-ins. Accountability.

self_attack_spiral.detected: The self-attack voice took over. It feels true but it's a trap.
self_attack_spiral.nextStep: Name the voice: 'That's the critic, not the truth.' See if naming creates distance.

perfectionism_trap.detected: All-or-nothing thinking collapsed partial progress into nothing.
perfectionism_trap.nextStep: Define 'enough' before you start tomorrow. Write it down. Stick to it.

overreach_collapse.detected: You tried to do everything and crashed. The full routine was too much.
overreach_collapse.nextStep: Tomorrow, start smaller. Ask: Is this the minimum viable version?

avoidance_at_threshold.detected: You couldn't cross the activation barrier. The gap was too wide.
avoidance_at_threshold.nextStep: Set up scaffolding tonight: one small thing in place to make tomorrow easier.
